headline: Apple is profitable again
text: At the Macworld show on 6 January Apple announced that it expects a profit of more than 45 million dollars on sales of about 1.575 billion for the quarter to December, its first good news in years. Jobs has cut the product line, ended the licensing of the Mac to clone makers and opened an online store.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/0000320193-98-000001.txt (Apple 8-K with press release of 6 January 1998, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Apple_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Asia's crisis deepens as Indonesia's rupiah collapses
text: Indonesia's rupiah fell 26 percent on 8 January to a record low, beyond 10,000 to the dollar; it has lost nearly 70 percent of its value since July. Jakarta residents emptied supermarket shelves, and on 15 January the government promised the IMF tougher reforms in return for the $43 billion rescue agreed last autumn. In Hong Kong, Peregrine, the largest Asian investment bank outside Japan, collapsed, brought down partly by Indonesian debt. With oil stocks swelling, Brent crude fell below $15 a barrel, a 45-month low. That is bad news for exporters such as Russia, where foreign investors are selling stocks and bonds: on 30 January its central bank raised its key rate from 28 to 42 percent.

headline: Netscape's first loss, layoffs, and a free browser
text: On 5 January Netscape warned that it would report a loss of $85 to $89 million for the fourth quarter, its first since going public, and its shares fell 20% to an all-time low. Browser revenue fell to $17 million from $52 million a year before, as Microsoft gives its browser away. On 22 January, with its browser share down to about 60%, Netscape said Navigator and Communicator will now be free, and that it will publish the program's source code. On 27 January it reported a quarterly loss of $88.3 million; about 300 jobs will go.

headline: Record year for Lehman
text: Lehman Brothers earned a record $647 million in the year to November 1997, in a year of near-record underwriting volumes and mergers on Wall Street.

headline: AOL raises its price, and its shares hit a high
text: On 9 February America Online said it will raise its unlimited monthly fee by 10%, to $21.95, from April. Its members now spend 23 hours a month online on average, against 7 hours before the flat rate, and every minute costs AOL money. Its shares jumped to a 52-week high on the news. AOL also cut 500 jobs at CompuServe, the rival online service it has just acquired, and made Robert Pittman president and chief executive of America Online, with founder Steve Case remaining chairman.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/02/09/technology/aol/ (CNNfn, 9 February 1998, read 2026-10-14); https://money.cnn.com/1998/01/30/technology/aol/ (CNNfn, 30 January 1998, on the CompuServe purchase, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Japan puts taxpayers' money into its big banks
text: Since the bubble burst in 1990, Japan's banks sit on a mountain of loans that will never be repaid, and in November several big financial firms collapsed. Until now the government did not dare to help with public money, because voters were furious when it rescued the housing lenders in 1996. That has changed: a law passed in February sets aside 30 trillion yen, and on 30 March all major banks, including IBJ, received a first 1.8 trillion yen of new capital from the state. Critics say the amount is far too small for the size of the losses.
source: https://www.bis.org/publications/paper-6-financial-crisis-japan-during-1990s-how-bank-japan-responded-and-lessons-learnt.pdf (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Faster than radio, faster than television: the internet reaches 70 million
text: It took radio 38 years to reach 50 million listeners and television 13 years to reach 50 million viewers. The internet did it in four, says a report the American government published on 15 April. At the end of 1997 about 70 million people were online, twice as many as a year before, and according to the report the traffic on the internet doubles every hundred days. Electronic commerce, it says, brings growth, well-paid jobs and lower inflation.
source: https://www.stackscale.com/blog/internet-evolution-statistics/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.allaboutmarketresearch.com/internet.htm (search result read 2026-10-04) (figures of Internet World Stats); https://hannemyr.com/en/diff.html (search result read 2026-10-04); https://library.unt.edu/gpo/oca/mrapr98.htm (search result read 2026-10-04)

headline: Netscape opens its code, and investors discover Netcenter
text: On 31 March Netscape put the source code of its next browser on the internet, free for any programmer to use and improve, under the name Mozilla. In April investors started to buy its shares again, for another reason: Netcenter, the web site that opens whenever someone starts Navigator, draws a huge amount of traffic, which puts Netscape in the same business as Yahoo!, Excite and Lycos, whose shares have soared. 'It is changing from a company that had been viewed as a failed competitor to Microsoft to a company in the same business as Yahoo,' said one fund manager.

headline: Amazon buys bookstores in Britain and Germany
text: On April 27 Amazon reported sales of $87.4 million for the first quarter, up 446% from a year earlier, and a net loss of $9.3 million. It has more than 2.26 million customer accounts. It announced the purchase of online booksellers in the UK and Germany and of the Internet Movie Database.

headline: Vickers accepts BMW's bid for Rolls-Royce
text: Vickers has accepted BMW's offer for the British luxury car maker Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, which already uses BMW engines; the price is 340 million pounds. Pischetsrieder promised to invest 1 billion pounds, double the workforce and triple production. Volkswagen is preparing a higher offer.

headline: Eleven countries qualify for the euro; Greece does not
text: On 3 May, at a summit in Brussels, EU leaders chose the eleven countries that will adopt the euro on 1 January 1999: Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Portugal, Finland, Ireland and Luxembourg. Belgium and Italy were let in although their government debts, about 122 percent of their annual economic output in 1997, are twice the 60 percent limit. Greece failed the tests: its 1997 deficit of 4.0 percent was above the 3 percent limit, and its inflation of 5.4 percent was far too high.

headline: Russia triples its key rate to 150 percent
text: Investors now call the rouble the rupiah of the Slavic world. Unsettled by Asia, a growing budget deficit, unpaid miners on strike and a plunge in oil prices, they are dumping Russian assets: the Moscow Times index of the 50 largest companies has lost about half its value this year, and buyers shun government Treasury bills, whose yields shot up to 80 percent. On 27 May the central bank tripled its key rate to 150 percent, having already spent reserves to defend the rouble. The government of Prime Minister Sergei Kiriyenko, 35, insists it will not devalue; Yeltsin has ordered spending cuts of more than $6.5 billion, and Russia hopes for more money from the IMF.

headline: Daimler-Benz and Chrysler agree to merge
text: On 7 May Daimler-Benz and the American car maker Chrysler signed a contract to merge into DaimlerChrysler, a deal valued at about 38 billion dollars, the largest cross-border merger ever. Schrempp calls it a merger of equals. The new company will build Mercedes, Chrysler, Jeep and Dodge cars.

headline: The American government sues Microsoft
text: On 18 May the Justice Department, twenty states and the District of Columbia took Microsoft to court. Almost every personal computer runs Microsoft's Windows, and the government says the company abuses that power to win the next market as well, the one for internet browsers: it builds its own Internet Explorer into Windows and stops computer makers from removing it or offering Netscape's Navigator instead. 'Microsoft follows the rules,' says Bill Gates, who denies that his company is a monopoly. Already in 1994 Microsoft had promised not to tie other products to Windows; it now argues that the browser is a feature of Windows, not a separate product.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_v._Microsoft_Corp. (read 2026-10-04)

text: Amazon began selling music CDs in June, its first big step beyond books. Investors are piling into internet shares.

headline: AOL pays $287 million for ICQ, a free chat program
text: America Online announced on 8 June that it has bought Mirabilis, an Israeli company whose free program ICQ tells users when their friends are online and lets them exchange messages instantly. AOL paid $287 million in cash and may pay up to $120 million more over three years if ICQ meets growth targets. ICQ, launched in November 1996, will stay a free service based in Tel Aviv with its own brand.

headline: UBS is born
text: The merger of the Bankgesellschaft and the Bankverein took legal effect on 27-28 June. The new UBS has total assets of more than $590 billion, making it the second-largest bank in the world. Each Bankverein share becomes 1 1/13 UBS shares and each Bankgesellschaft bearer share five shares of the new bank.

headline: A $22.6 billion rescue for Russia brings only brief relief
text: On 13 July the IMF, the World Bank and Japan announced loans of $22.6 billion to Russia through 1999 to defend the rouble, in return for spending cuts and tax reforms. Yields on Russian Treasury bills, about 120 percent early in the month, halved the next day. But the Duma rejected part of the tax package, so the IMF cut its first payment from $5.6 billion to $4.8 billion, and by 24 July yields were back up to 66 percent. In New York the S&P 500 closed at a record 1,186.69 on 17 July. By 31 July, worried about Japan and slowing profits, it had fallen to 1,120.67.

headline: Enron bids for Britain's Wessex Water
text: Enron is forming a global water company and has made an all-cash offer for Wessex Water, a British water utility, valued at about $2.9 billion. Enron believes water is the next utility market to be opened to competition.
source: https://enroncorp.com/corp/pressroom/releases/1998/press_chron1998 (Enron press release, 24 July 1998; read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enron (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Russia defaults and the crisis goes global
text: On 17 August Russia devalued the rouble, defaulted on its domestic debt and stopped paying foreign creditors, a month after a $22.6 billion IMF and World Bank package. The Asian crisis and falling commodity prices had drained its reserves. Investors are fleeing risky markets everywhere.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Russian_financial_crisis (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Small depositors queue outside a Moscow bank to get their savings out as the rouble collapses, 8 September 1998

headline: UBS caught in the LTCM collapse
text: Long-Term Capital Management's equity fell from $2.3 billion to about $400 million in three weeks. The hedge fund in Greenwich, Connecticut, founded in 1994 by the bond trader John Meriwether, with the Nobel prize winners Myron Scholes and Robert Merton on its board, had borrowed more than $124 billion on top of $4.7 billion of its own money to bet that small price gaps between bonds would close. Russia's default in August set off its losses. On 23 September the New York Fed organised a $3.625 billion rescue by 14 banks, UBS and Credit Suisse among those putting in $300 million each. UBS has its own large exposure through an option deal on LTCM shares struck in 1997. On 30 September UBS shares fell 14% in a day as investors lost confidence in the leadership; an internal investigation is due to report on Friday.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management (read 2026-10-03); Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 1 October 1998, p. 35 ('Weitere Verluste der UBS-Valoren'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1998-10-01.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/ubs-ag (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management (re-read 2026-10-04)

headline: eBay, the online auction site, goes public
text: eBay of San Jose sold 3.5 million shares on the Nasdaq; on the first day they closed at nearly three times the issue price, valuing the company at nearly $1.9 billion. eBay runs a website where people auction goods to each other, from Beanie Babies to collectibles, and takes a fee on each sale. It had more than 1 million registered users at the end of August and, unlike most internet companies, it makes a profit. The existing shareholders, led by founder Pierre Omidyar, hold 24.5 million of the 39.7 million shares and have agreed not to sell for only 120 days, so from late January they will be free to sell.

headline: Hopes of a rate cut bring internet shares roaring back
text: On 4 September Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said the American economy could not remain untouched while the rest of the world slows down. Investors took it as a hint that interest rates may be cut, and on 8 September the Dow Jones index rose 380 points, its biggest one-day gain ever. Internet shares, the market's most volatile, rebounded hardest after their sharp fall, and America Online's shares were among the biggest gainers.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/09/08/markets/marketwrap/ (CNNfn, 8 September 1998, read 2026-10-14)
imageCaption: The words 'Federal Reserve' above the entrance of the Fed's building in Washington

headline: Citicorp and Travelers become Citigroup
text: The merger of Citicorp, owner of Citibank, and Travelers Group, owner of the Travelers insurance business and the brokerage Salomon Smith Barney, was completed on 8 October, creating Citigroup, the world's largest financial services company. John Reed of Citicorp and Sanford Weill of Travelers run it together as co-chairmen and co-chief executives. Combining a bank with an insurer breaks the Depression-era Glass-Steagall rules; the Federal Reserve has granted a temporary waiver, and the company expects Congress to change the law. Salomon closed its bond arbitrage desk in July and was among the firms that put money into the rescue of the hedge fund Long-Term Capital Management in September.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramm%E2%80%93Leach%E2%80%93Bliley_Act (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management (read 2026-10-03)

headline: The yen leaps; Japan nationalises a failing bank
text: On 7 October the dollar fell from about 134 to 120 yen, the biggest daily move since the yen began to float in 1973, as hedge funds wound down bets financed with cheap yen. It fell to about 117 by the month's end. On 23 October the Diet nationalised the Long-Term Credit Bank under a new law that also offers public money to sound banks.

headline: A surprise Fed cut on 15 October and shares bounce 8 percent
text: Shares fell further in early October, then on 15 October the Federal Reserve cut its key rate again, to about 5 percent, without waiting for a meeting. The market rallied strongly after mid-October as fears of a financial breakdown eased. The S&P 500 rose 8% in October to 1,098.67. The numbers: the Fed's rate 5 percent. Inflation 1.5 percent. Unemployment 4.6 percent.

headline: Nokia passes Motorola as the world's biggest phone maker
text: On 23 October Nokia reported third-quarter pre-tax profit up 85% and sales up 62%, far better than expected, and said it is now the world's largest maker of mobile phones, ahead of Motorola. Sales rose in the US, Europe and China.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/10/23/companies/nokia/ via web.archive.org (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia (read 2026-10-03)

headline: AOL buys Netscape and teams up with Sun
text: America Online, with 14 million subscribers, agreed on 24 November to buy Netscape for shares worth $4.2 billion, gaining the Navigator browser and Netcenter, one of the ten most-visited web sites. In a separate three-year alliance, AOL will buy $500 million of computers and services from Sun Microsystems, and Sun will pay AOL more than $350 million in licence, marketing and advertising fees. AOL will keep shipping Microsoft's Internet Explorer with its software. Its shares rose on the news.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/11/24/technology/aol/ (CNNfn, 24 November 1998, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Third rate cut; Wall Street recovers
text: The Federal Reserve has now cut interest rates three times since the end of September, and central banks in Europe have followed. Stocks have recovered most of the summer's losses, and the market for new share issues has reopened. Lehman's shares rose another third in November.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/0001047469-99-007702.txt (Lehman 10-K fiscal 1998: three Fed cuts, S&P 500 up 22% from 31 August to 30 November; read 2026-10-03)

headline: Daimler-Benz and Chrysler become DaimlerChrysler
text: The German Daimler-Benz and the American Chrysler Corporation have merged into a new company, DaimlerChrysler AG, whose share began trading in Frankfurt and New York on 17 November. Daimler-Benz shareholders swap each of their shares for 1.005 DaimlerChrysler shares, and more than 98% of them tendered their shares in the exchange offer; Chrysler holders receive 0.6235 DaimlerChrysler shares for each Chrysler share. The former Daimler-Benz shareholders own about 58% of the new company, the former Chrysler shareholders about 42%. Stock markets have recovered from the summer's Russian crisis.

headline: The Master Settlement: 206 billion dollars to the states
text: On 23 November the four largest US cigarette makers, Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds, Brown & Williamson and Lorillard, signed the Master Settlement Agreement with 46 states and several territories. They will pay at least 206 billion dollars over the first 25 years and accept limits on marketing; in return the states drop their claims for smoking-related health costs.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobacco_Master_Settlement_Agreement (read 2026-10-03)

headline: 1998 in review: a panic in the middle, up 27 percent in the end
text: The S&P 500 rose 27% in 1998 to 1,229.23, after first closing above 1,000 on 2 February and falling 15% in August alone. The Dow passed 9,000 on 6 April and ended at 9,181.43, up 16.1%. The Fed's autumn rate cuts brought the buyers back.

headline: AOL joins the S&P 500 and its shares soar
text: On 22 December Standard & Poor's said America Online will join its index of 500 leading American shares, replacing Venator, the former Woolworth's. AOL's shares jumped more than 13% in trading after the close, and Deutsche Bank raised its price target the next morning. Funds that track the index must now buy the shares. AOL was worth about $41 billion at the time, making it one of the most valuable companies on the New York Stock Exchange; the new member gives the old index a technology slant.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/12/22/markets/afterbell/ (CNNfn, 22 December 1998, read 2026-10-14); https://money.cnn.com/1998/12/23/companies/aol/ (CNNfn, 23 December 1998, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Analyst predicts $400 for Amazon
text: Henry Blodget, an internet analyst, predicted that Amazon's shares, trading at about $240, would reach $400 within a year. Many investors thought the forecast absurd for a company that has never made a profit.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Blodget (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Netscape rises with America Online
text: Since the takeover agreement each Netscape share stands for 0.45 America Online share, so Netscape's price now follows AOL's. And AOL's shares soared in December. On 22 December Standard & Poor's said it would add America Online to its index of 500 leading shares, replacing Venator, the former Woolworth's; AOL's shares jumped more than 13% in trading after the close. Index funds must buy the shares of companies that join the index.
source: https://money.cnn.com/1998/11/24/technology/aol/ (CNNfn, 24 November 1998, read 2026-10-14); https://money.cnn.com/1998/12/22/markets/afterbell/ (CNNfn, 22 December 1998, read 2026-10-14); https://money.cnn.com/1998/12/23/companies/aol/ (CNNfn, 23 December 1998, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Asia's crisis forces Boeing to cut production
text: On 1 December Boeing said it will cut production of the 747 from 3.5 to 2 planes a month in late 1999, and possibly to 1, and slow the 757, 767 and 777 too. 'The economic slowdown in Asia is driving air traffic down,' said Alan Mulally, head of commercial airplanes.
source: https://boeing.mediaroom.com/1998-12-01-Boeing-Announces-Production-Rate-Changes-Financial-Projections (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Wal-Mart is the best stock in the Dow
text: Wal-Mart shares have about doubled in 1998, after rising some 70% in 1997, making it the best performer in the Dow Jones Industrial Average this year. Comparable-store sales are growing faster than last year, and the company bought back about 1.2 billion dollars of its own shares.
source: Wal-Mart Stores 1999 Annual Report, letter and Q&A with David Glass, https://stock.walmart.com/_assets/_46796feebc5ddf6d2adbeabac9558ae9/walmart/db/950/9626/annual_report/1999-annual-report-for-walmart-stores-inc_130199459840185623.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2008/11/06/wal-mart-reports-october-1998-sales (search result summary read 2026-10-03)

headline: Exxon and Mobil agree to merge
text: On 1 December Exxon agreed to buy Mobil in a share deal valued at about 76 to 79 billion dollars, the biggest US corporate combination ever: each Mobil share becomes 1.32015 Exxon shares, and Exxon's owners will hold about 70 percent. The deal reunites two pieces of Rockefeller's Standard Oil and needs regulators' approval. With crude below 11 dollars a barrel, the companies plan to cut 9,000 jobs and save 2.8 billion dollars a year. Lee Raymond will run the combined company.
source: https://dieselnet.com/news/1998/12exxon.php (read 2026-10-03); https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1998-12-02-1998336042-story.html (read 2026-10-03); Exxon Form 8-K of 1 December 1998, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/0000950103-98-001038.txt (read 2026-10-03)
